How to Design and Install a Quality Skylight for Your Home

Roofing information archive
Home improvement tips

The roof is an often neglected piece of real estate, but a skylight can dramatically change the look and feel of a room. Designing a skylight involves more than just cutting a rectangular hole in the ceiling and installing a window. Consider these tips for installing the right skylight with an experienced roofing contractor.

Placement
The sun isn’t a static source of light, and the location of the skylight in respect to the direction of the sun will have a major impact on how the light interacts with the rest of the room. In general, south-facing skylights will receive more light from the sun and will likely increase the temperature by a few degrees; in exchange, you can enjoy a vivid and natural glow throughout most of the day. North-facing skylights are more suited for soft, diffused lighting.

Glass Type
UV exposure and heating and cooling costs are two major considerations when it comes to designing an energy-efficient skylight. A skylight will likely result in a slight bump in energy costs, but glazed glass or accessories such as blinds and shades can help control energy costs. Additionally, UV lighting can damage wood and some types of furniture over time, so it’s worthwhile to consider tinted or coated windows to block UV rays.

Size
Most of the expenses associated a skylight lie in installation, rather than material costs. It’s generally worthwhile to consider the overall aesthetic enhancement of a larger skylight rather than the initial cost-savings of a smaller installation. Alternatively, a tubular installation for a bathroom or other small area can capture lots of sunlight and provide a cost-effective alternative to a full-size skylight.

Why Should You Have Your Chimney Inspected?

Roofing information archive
Home improvement tips

Annual chimney inspections will ensure that your fireplace and chimney are in safe condition to be used for your home heating needs. Each year, tens of thousands of residential fires are started by fires in the fireplace. By having your chimney inspected, you can greatly reduce the risk of a fire caused by your fireplace or chimney. During an inspection, a technician will make sure that there is no soot built up in your chimney, and will also ensure that your chimney has not suffered any structural damage. By scheduling this procedure once a year, you will help to improve the safety of your home.

Exploring the Benefits of Installing an Energy-Saving Roof

Roofing information archive
Home improvement tips

Eventually, even the most well-constructed roof will require replacement. If it’s time to replace your home’s roof, you may consider installing a roof that is constructed using energy-saving materials. Along with helping to reduce your monthly energy bills, an energy-saving roof offers many benefits to the homeowner. Let’s explore some of the great benefits of installing an energy-saving roof.

Reflect Heat and Sunlight
During the hot summer months, a conventional roof will absorb sunlight and heat. This heat is then transferred to your home, which will cause your living spaces to heat up. When you choose reflective materials for your energy-saving roof, your roof will reflect the sun’s rays. By reflecting, rather than absorbing, sunlight, your energy-saving roof will help to keep your home cooler during the hot summer months.

More Efficient Heating and Cooling
An energy-efficient roof will make your home heating and cooling system more efficient, all year round. Your energy-efficient roof will be constructed using insulation materials that will help to maintain the temperature of your home. With increased insulation, your roof will help keep your home cooler in the summertime, and warmer in the winter.

Great Financial Incentives
Along with making your home more comfortable, an energy-saving roof will help reduce your monthly energy bill. In certain parts of the country, you may also be eligible for a tax rebate or other financial incentives when you install an energy-efficient roof.

A Homeowner's Guide to the Most Common Home Roofing Materials

Roofing information archive
Home improvement tips

When it comes time to replace your home’s aging roof, you will have many different materials to choose from. Roofing materials are available in a variety of styles and colors, and a carefully chosen material can provide a great accent to your home’s exterior. If you are choosing between different materials for your next roofing project, consult this homeowner’s guide to the most popular roofing materials.

Composition Shingles
Composition shingles will provide a clean and classic look to your home’s roof. Available in a variety of colors and sizes, composition shingles are a versatile choice for many home roofing projects. These shingles are durable, affordable, and long-lasting, making them a great option for many homeowners.

Metal
Metal can be used to create an attractive and energy-efficient roof. Typically, metal roofs are made of standing-seam steel, but they can also be constructed of other metals such as copper and zinc. Standing-seam steel roofs are composed of recycled materials, making them a great option for the environmentally conscious homeowner.

Concrete
Concrete can be molded into a variety of shapes and sizes of roofing shingles. This type of home roofing material is extremely weather-resistant, long-lasting, and easy to maintain. Concrete shingles can be styled to look like a variety of other materials, such as wood, slate, and tile.

Wood Shakes
Wood shakes are a classic home roofing material, and are often made from the heart of a cedar tree. With a variety of wood styles to choose from, wood shakes can be used to create a beautiful and natural-looking roof.
